entities.summary:
The Vienna offensive was a pivotal 1945 military operation that took place in Vienna, marking a turning point in the Battle of Vienna. 

 The operation, which lasted from April 2 to April 13, 1945, involved the Soviet Red Army, led by Marshal Georgy Zhukov, and the German Wehrmacht, under the command of General Rudolf Knoll. The offensive was a crucial moment in the Allied victory, paving the way for the Soviet capture of Vienna and the eventual defeat of Nazi Germany. 

 The Vienna offensive had significant consequences, with the Soviet Union emerging as a dominant world power and the beginning of the Cold War. The operation also led to the end of World War II in Europe and the beginning of the post-war era. 

 As Marshal Zhukov noted, 'The capture of Vienna was a major victory for the Soviet Union, and marked a significant turning point in the war.'
